stem: Choose the best way to combine: 'Himani was very nervous. She delivered a great presentation.'
options: Himani was very nervous because she delivered a great presentation.
Though Himani was very nervous, she delivered a great presentation.
Himani was very nervous unless she delivered a great presentation.
Himani was very nervous where she delivered a great presentation.
explanation: Correct option: (B). The two ideas contrast: she was nervous, yet she did well, so 'though' (contrast) is the right conjunction. stem: In 'Though seriously wounded in this encounter, he continued to fight alongside his comrades', what meaning does the conjunction add, and which part is the main clause?
options: Cause or reason; 'Though seriously wounded in this encounter'
Time and sequence; 'he continued to fight alongside his comrades'
Aim or purpose; 'Though seriously wounded in this encounter'
Contrast; 'he continued to fight alongside his comrades'
explanation: Correct option: (D). 'Though' signals contrast: fighting on is unexpected after being wounded. The part that makes complete sense on its own, 'he continued to fight alongside his comrades', is the main clause; the 'though' part depends on it and is the subordinate clause. Reason, time and purpose are the meanings of 'because', 'when' and 'so that'.

stem: The captain said to the coach, "Our team won the championship last year." Complete the indirect speech: The captain told the coach that ______.

their team will win the championship the following year
their team has won the championship in the last year

explanation: Correct option: (D). In indirect speech 'our' changes to 'their', the simple past 'won' shifts back to the past perfect 'had won', and 'last year' becomes 'the previous year'. stem: He said, "I am reading this book here today." Which indirect form makes every change correctly?
options: He said that he is reading this book here today.
He said that I was reading that book there that day.

explanation: Correct option: (C).
